title: Security Log Analyzer & Alert Triage Dashboard
disclaimer: Alerts in this report are DETECTION INDICATORS produced by rule-based analysis of the supplied logs. They are not confirmed attacks and require analyst validation. MITRE ATT&CK mappings mean the observed behaviour is consistent with a technique, not that the technique was proven. No IP addresses were scanned or blocked.

detection_rules.name: Repeated Failed Login Attempts
detection_rules.description: Many failed logins from the same source IP in a short time window.
detection_rules.logic: Groups auth_failure events by source IP and slides a time window over them. Alerts when the peak count inside the window reaches the threshold.
detection_rules.severity_logic: Medium when peak >= threshold; High when peak >= high threshold.
detection_rules.mitre_note: Repeated password failures from one source are the defining behaviour of password guessing.

detection_rules.name: Successful Login After Repeated Failures
detection_rules.description: A successful login from an IP that just produced several failed logins.
detection_rules.logic: For each auth_success, counts auth_failure events from the same IP in the preceding window.
detection_rules.severity_logic: High by default; Critical when failures >= brute-force threshold and target the same account.
detection_rules.mitre_note: Failures followed by success can indicate a guessed password now being used as a valid account.

detection_rules.name: Multiple Accounts Targeted From One IP
detection_rules.description: Failed logins against many different usernames from a single source IP.
detection_rules.logic: Counts distinct usernames among auth_failure events per IP in a sliding window.
detection_rules.severity_logic: High when distinct accounts >= threshold; Critical if any login from that IP succeeded in/after the window.
detection_rules.mitre_note: Few attempts across many accounts from one source matches password spraying. (Credential stuffing, T1110.004, cannot be distinguished from logs alone.)

detection_rules.name: Unusual Login Time
detection_rules.description: Successful login outside configured business hours (UTC) or on a weekend.
detection_rules.logic: Compares the hour/weekday of each auth_success event timestamp with the configured business hours.
detection_rules.severity_logic: Low by default; Medium for privileged accounts (e.g. root, admin).
detection_rules.mitre_note: No ATT&CK technique is assigned: login time alone does not show how access was obtained.

detection_rules.name: Watchlisted Source IP Activity
detection_rules.description: Activity from an IP or CIDR range present in the local watchlist.
detection_rules.logic: Matches every event's validated source IP against the configured local watchlist. No external lookups, scans, or blocking are performed.
detection_rules.severity_logic: Low for any activity; Medium if failures/4xx errors; High if a login succeeded.
detection_rules.mitre_note: No technique is assigned: a watchlist match is reputation context, not evidence of a technique.

detection_rules.name: Repeated HTTP 401/403 Responses
detection_rules.description: Many HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden) responses for one client IP.
detection_rules.logic: Slides a time window over 401/403 responses per IP and alerts when the peak reaches the threshold.
detection_rules.severity_logic: Medium when peak >= threshold; High when peak >= 2x threshold.
detection_rules.mitre_note: T1110 is assigned only when most failures are 401s on login/auth endpoints; 403s on other paths are access-control denials and receive no technique.

detection_rules.name: Suspicious HTTP Request Pattern
detection_rules.description: Path enumeration, probing of sensitive files, or exploit-like request strings.
detection_rules.logic: Per IP and time window: many distinct paths with mostly 4xx responses (enumeration), requests for >= 2 sensitive paths (e.g. /.env, /.git/config), or traversal/injection patterns.
detection_rules.severity_logic: Medium for enumeration or sensitive-path probing; High when traversal/injection patterns are present.
detection_rules.mitre_note: Enumeration and sensitive-path probing map to Wordlist Scanning; exploit-like strings map to an *attempt* at Exploit Public-Facing Application. Neither confirms success.
